scores.rationale: Mechanisms (sync switch before failover, reverse replication, DAG/Data Guard) are accurate; minor issues like DNS-flip claims for interfaces and the "no downtime" versus 60 s pause framing are handled honestly.

scores.evidence: Move a working, on-premises patient scheduling system ... Users must not lose scheduling at any point.
scores.rationale: Solves the real problem with staged tier-by-tier migration and explicitly reframes zero downtime as a ≤60 s pause; some gaps on kiosks/SMS detail and clinical cutover comms.

scores.evidence: Exactly one writable primary database at all times. On-premises is the system of record until the Phase 3 cutover, the cloud after it. Never both.
scores.rationale: Single write authority, rollback, coexistence, and exceptions are consistently honored across decisions, phases, validation and cross-cutting tables.

scores.rationale: Validation is tied to specific risks, early (V0, V1), thresholds labeled as assumptions, with post-cutover reconciliation; production monitoring continues though load-test realism could improve.
